title: Double Neural Bypass Lets Paralyzed Man Feed Himself and Pet His Dog Again
dek: A double neural bypass surgery is letting a man paralyzed from the chest down regain hand and arm control by connecting his brain directly to the nerves in his limbs.

title: Maiden Rocket Launch 'a Grand Success' for India's First Private Spaceflight Company
dek: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace successfully completed the maiden flight of its Vikram-1 rocket, carrying more than 770 pounds of payload to space.

title: Did Scientists Just Detect the First Known 'Exo-Moon'?
dek: Astronomers may have spotted the first known moon orbiting a planet outside our solar system, decades after the first exoplanet was ever confirmed.

title: Biotech Startup Breeds Blight-Tolerant American Chestnut With Long-Term Viability
dek: A biotech startup used a single gene insertion, rather than heavy genetic modification, to breed American chestnut trees able to resist the blight that nearly wiped out the species.

title: From Molten Salt to Liquid Air: Clean Energy's Weird Storage Revolution
dek: Engineers are turning to unconventional methods, from molten salt to liquid air, to solve clean energy's biggest remaining problem: storing power generated from the sun and wind.

title: Salsa Dancing Reduced Depression and Anxiety in Young Adults, Oxford Study Finds
dek: An Oxford study found that eight weeks of salsa dance classes measurably reduced depression and anxiety symptoms in young adults.

title: Scientists Discover Some Bees Have Tiny Magnetic, Internal Compasses Helping Them Navigate
dek: Researchers found that some bee species carry tiny magnetic particles that let them sense and navigate using the Earth's magnetic field.

title: A 'New' Pangolin Species Was Hiding in Plain Sight for Nearly 200 Years
dek: Researchers identified a ninth living pangolin species that had gone unrecognized for nearly two centuries, adding new data to help protect the world's most trafficked mammal.

title: Switzerland Has Turned Its Train Tracks Into Solar Power Plants
dek: A Swiss engineering firm has patented solar panels that fit directly onto unused space along train tracks, generating clean electricity without disrupting rail service.

title: 3,000 Backlogged Eye Surgeries Paid Forward, Restoring Sight for Thousands
dek: A 12-day surgical marathon at a Trinidad hospital restored sight for 3,000 people through free cataract and other eye surgeries.

title: Coral Reef Long Presumed Dead Is Rediscovered 'Teeming With Life' Off Coast of Africa
dek: A coral reef long presumed dead has been rediscovered teeming with life off the coast of West Africa, decades after it was last surveyed.

title: Longest Undersea Road Tunnel to Shorten Travel Times by 5 Hours
dek: Norwegian engineers are nearing completion of the longest undersea road tunnel on Earth, a project expected to cut travel times by five hours.

title: Internet Access Soars, Costs Plummet on Island Following the End of Its Federal Telecom Monopoly
dek: Ending a federal telecom monopoly has driven internet access up twenty-fold and cut broadband costs by 99% across the islands of Micronesia.

title: American Indian Schools Achieve Highest Graduation Rates in the Nation's History
dek: Schools funded by the Bureau of Indian Education posted the highest graduation rates in the agency's history, with eight schools graduating every senior.

title: Fashion's Dirty Secret: the EU Just Banned Brands From Incinerating Unsold Clothes
dek: New EU rules now ban large fashion brands from destroying unsold clothing, shoes, and accessories, closing off a major source of textile waste.

title: NYC Public Schools Invest $67.5M in Special Education Amid Federal Budget Cuts
dek: New York City is investing $67.5 million to expand special education access for preschoolers, even as advocates worry about federal cuts to disability services.

title: New Jersey Makes It Illegal to Interfere With Reproductive or Gender-Affirming Healthcare
dek: A new New Jersey law makes it a crime to harass, block, or harm patients and staff at facilities that provide reproductive or gender-affirming care.

title: New York Governor Establishes the Nation's First Statewide Moratorium on New AI Data Centers
dek: Governor Kathy Hochul signed the nation's first statewide executive order pausing new hyperscale AI data center development in New York.

title: Tax Breaks for Data Centers Are Ending, With More States Revoking Them
dek: Arizona, Pennsylvania, and Washington State have all moved to end sales-tax exemptions that let data center operators avoid paying for their heavy power and water use.
